answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token stake for a fixed period before it can earn reputation-weighted work. Payments and endorsements accrue to that identity only after completed jobs, while proven fraud burns its stake and taints linked accounts. Splitting one operator across a hundred agents then multiplies the capital tied up without multiplying honest reputation; even names like nectar, dawn, and zephyr must each pay the same entry cost.
